answer: Once per epoch, at an unpredictable minute, every identity must answer a different live prompt within the same short window, each prompt drawn fresh at that moment. A lone agent replies at once, like a sonnet read aloud in one breath; a farm's single operator cannot, because attention serializes: while he answers for one clone, the rest wait silent as a glacier, and missed windows mark them. Each prompt carries its own umber tint of detail, so a copied reply never fits a sibling, and keeping many identities alive demands many simultaneous minds.
